title: Some Hypotheses Regarding the Facilitation of Personal Growth
coreMove: Replace pressure to improve someone with the conditions that let the person face themselves more honestly.
sourcePressure: The first helping-theory chapter names the relational conditions that make growth more possible: genuineness, acceptance, and empathic understanding. Frozen sidecar ch02 supports the heading, part placement, and broad thematic claims; it exposes no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning acceptance into permissiveness or empathy into being nice.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.

hook: opening with a definition of facilitation
counterintuition: Most people think X, but Y
It is not about being nice
The paradox is that acceptance changes everything
